howTheMeasurementWasTaken.renderer: pdftoppm -r 600 -gray, PGM (P5) single channel. Not -png: a -gray -png render emits an RGB PNG that a naive grayscale reader misreads silently, so the raw single-channel PGM is read directly instead.
howTheMeasurementWasTaken.darkPixel: grey strictly less than the published threshold, of 255. Counts are published at 128, 160 and 200 wherever a grey fill is in scope, because a threshold choice can hide or invent a fill.
howTheMeasurementWasTaken.scope: the widget's own /Rect, converted from PDF user space at 600/72 with the page height taken from the MediaBox (792pt on every page of both families).
howTheMeasurementWasTaken.positiveControl: On the COURT'S OWN SOURCE, annotations-on minus annotations-hidden at each button rect. The buttons are LIVE WIDGETS there, so a non-zero delta proves the render draws the ink being counted. It is non-zero on all nineteen widgets.
howTheMeasurementWasTaken.whatIsNotANegativeControl: The same annotations-on vs annotations-hidden comparison on the DELIVERED pre-repair bytes reads IDENTICALLY both ways, on every page and at every threshold. That is NOT a negative control. It is the proof the caption had been flattened into page CONTENT and would print from any viewer and off any printer however it handles annotations. VF44 corrected exactly this labelling in FIX143's work.
howTheMeasurementWasTaken.overSuppressionControl: With annotations hidden, the court's own page reads 0 dark pixels inside all nineteen rectangles at thresholds 128, 160 and 200. The paper under every button is blank, so what was withdrawn is viewer chrome and not one mark of the form.

whichPagesTheCaptionsWereActuallyOn.answer: Fifteen of the seventeen are on a document a clerk stamps and a judge reads. Two are on the guidance sheet. The defect is therefore not a cover-page artefact and the repair is not discretionary.

rows.whatWasActuallyWrong: Each CXP source ships the issuer's viewer chrome as /Ff 65536 push buttons in the page's bottom margin. form.updateFieldAppearances() regenerates each one's appearance from its /MK /CA caption and form.flatten() then draws that appearance onto the page through the widget's own /P, so the caption became page CONTENT. FIX06 declared all seventeen in the field map months ago and said in the map's own reason text that the flattener carried them onto the page. Declaring a caption does not stop it printing.
rows.howThisDiffersFromConnecticut: FIX143 repaired the same CLASS with detachNestedControlFields and suppressSynthesizedAppearances at a finalizeOfficialForm call site. Neither flag is reachable here: this builder does not call finalizeOfficialForm at all, it drives pdf-lib directly. The mechanism differs too -- Connecticut's controls hang below a NESTED AcroForm root, which is what detachNestedControlFields exists for, while all seventeen of these sit DIRECTLY in the AcroForm's own /Fields array, where a flat detachment reaches them. Verified field by field: inFlatFieldsArray true on all seventeen.
rows.repair: In the builder, not the output. A family-local opt-in constant DETACH_SOURCE_FORM_CONTROLS detaches the seventeen push buttons BEFORE updateFieldAppearances and BEFORE flatten. No shared module was touched and no shared default moved. A builder-side guard asserts, after flatten, that no detached control's appearance stream is still referenced from any page's /Resources /XObject -- proof the detachment reached the page rather than a report that it was attempted -- and a second assertion holds the per-document counts (3/3/2/3/3/3).

theFailureModeThatCaughtConnecticut.what: FIX143's PDF repair was correct and its family still FAILED, because two delivered artifacts kept asserting the defect after it was gone and neither digest moved. Every artifact in both of these families was swept for sentences describing the captions.
theFailureModeThatCaughtConnecticut.whatWasFound: The only delivered artifact in either family that described the defect was production-field-map.json. Its seventeen (Illinois) and two (Kentucky) refusal rows carried the reason text 'flatten() carries the source's own button caption into the delivered page' and, on Illinois, the flag sourceAuthoredInk: true. BOTH were repaired in this same commit: the reason text now says the control is detached before flatten so the delivered page carries no button caption, sourceAuthoredInk is false, and a new controlDetachedBeforeFlatten: true records what was actually done. The builder self-test was inverted to match -- it now asserts 17 rows detached and ZERO rows claiming ink, where it used to assert 17 rows claiming ink.
theFailureModeThatCaughtConnecticut.whatWasNotFound: Neither participant-instructions.md nor filing-instructions.md in either family ever mentioned the buttons, and neither family carries an independent-visual-review.json. So there is no Connecticut-shaped stale instruction here. That is a finding, not an absence of work: it was grepped for.
theFailureModeThatCaughtConnecticut.theOneFileWhoseDigestDidNotMoveAndShould: reports/actual-writes.json published refusedFieldsWithInk as a LITERAL empty array while all seventeen Illinois refusals carried sourceAuthoredInk: true -- the report contradicted the map beside it and nothing compared them. It is now DERIVED from the map. Its VALUE is still [], so that field alone would have moved no digest -- which is exactly the shape of the trap: a reader diffing digests would have concluded nothing changed there. What changed is that the empty array is now the map's own answer instead of a literal, and a new self-test assertion compares them on every build. The file's digest did move in this commit, but for a different reason -- the three unmeasured byte-reading counters below -- so the digest is not evidence that this particular field was looked at.

aThirdThingWorthSaying.what: Both families were carrying published measurements that had never been taken, on a terminal family, with every counter green.
theCounters: reports/build-summary.json on KENTUCKY published eight literal zeros beside one null for the nine completeness counters. This builder counts none of the nine. Illinois had already been corrected to nine nulls with a note; Kentucky had not. It is nine nulls now, with the same note. A counter that could not be measured is null, never 0.

reports/actual-writes.json on BOTH families published addedGlyphsReadFromOutputBytes: 0 -- while every packet adds glyphs at every write -- and nonWhitespaceGlyphsOutsideMeasuredWriteBoxes: 0, and republished the WRITE COUNT under the name flattenedWidgetAppearancesReadFromOutputBytes, which is not the number of appearances flatten() draws. Three field names promise a reading of the output bytes; all three were literals. They are null now, with a note naming scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-output-glyph-reading.mjs, which reads these properly and which neither builder calls.
aThirdThingWorthSaying.whyThisIsTheSameDefectAsTheCaption: A caption in the field map still prints, and a zero in a report still reads as a clean measurement. Both are a document saying something about the artifact that nobody checked against the artifact.

aThirdThingWorthSaying.andTheRasterGate: The Illinois RASTER_PASS measured 22 pages of paper geometry on bytes that were stamping 'PRINT FORM' onto the proposed order. That is not a fault in the raster gate -- it measures what it measures -- but it is worth stating plainly that RASTER_PASS on a family is not evidence that the pages carry no form-control chrome.
